_comment: Short 4 in docs/CONTENT.md: a charge your insurance has never seen. The first line is carried in `variants` because tts.mjs treats that as the hook.
_injury: A bee sting: small, and it still produces a line nobody can explain. The swollen hand is the joke and the reason for the visit in one line.
_lessons: Written after the 2026-09-17 rewrites. Opens on the surprise (three charges on the bill, two on the letter) in the second line; names the word, pending, by about 0:12 and defines it in the same breath; one idea (timing), no second concept; top to bottom.
_numbers: One figure only, the $100 shot. The other rows carry no amounts, because the point is which row is missing, not what the rows add up to.
_accuracy: Says 'usually', not 'always'. A charge missing from the EOB is most often a claim still in process or one sent at a different time; it can also be something never submitted, which the phone question in h7 catches either way.

variants.bee: A bee stung you, and your hand swelled up like a rubber glove. So you go to your doctor.

body.text: The bill lists three charges. Your insurance letter lists two.
The shot, a hundred dollars, is not on the letter at all.
That is usually not a mistake. It is pending. Your insurance just has not finished with it yet.
Charges can reach your insurance at different times, and one can run weeks behind the rest.
So do not pay that line yet. Wait for the letter that lists it.
Or call and ask one question. Has this been sent to my insurance?
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.
